Research Focus

Our Research Areas

Our research spans a broad spectrum of statistical and actuarial disciplines, united by the goal of advancing quantitative risk assessment methodologies.

🌡️
Climate Risk Modelling
Developing spatial and temporal models for extreme weather events, seasonal forecasting, and climate-resilient insurance pricing across African regions. This includes heatwaves, drought, and flood risk assessment.
🧠
Machine Learning & AI
Applying deep learning, neural networks, and ensemble methods to insurance and health datasets for improved prediction and risk classification. We explore supervised and unsupervised learning for actuarial applications.
🏥
Health & Survival Analysis
Studying mortality trends, infectious disease dynamics, and longevity risk using survival analysis and machine learning methods. This includes under-five mortality, maternal health, and Bayesian mortality projections.
🗺️
Spatial Statistics
Using geostatistical methods, kriging, and spatial copula frameworks for environmental monitoring, regional risk mapping, and wastewater surveillance. This includes Bayesian spatial modelling for public health and insurance.
📊
Data Visualisation
Developing multivariate visualisation techniques including biplots, principal surfaces, and goodness-of-fit diagnostics. This includes interactive dashboards using RShiny for exploring high-dimensional data.
🛡️
Risk & Insurance Analytics
Developing pricing, reserving, and capital assessment models for general and life insurance. This includes catastrophe modelling, dependence structures, and stochastic simulations for portfolio risk.
📐
Multivariate Methods
Extending classical multivariate techniques to high-dimensional settings, including Generalised Singular Value Decomposition (GSVD) approaches to MANOVA and Canonical Variate Analysis, with applications to complex actuarial and financial data.
⚡
Energy & Financial Forecasting
Developing multivariate time series methods for forecasting electricity prices, demand, and financial market variables in South African and African markets. This includes regime-switching models and dependence structures in energy portfolios.
Current Work

Projects in Progress

The lab is establishing its research programme. Current student projects are underway, with outputs expected in the coming years.

Climate Risk and Insurance Pricing

Odey Mofokeng (MSc Statistics) is developing Bayesian spatial copula frameworks for insurance pricing in KwaZulu-Natal, examining flood and drought risk through geostatistical methods. Expected completion: December 2026

Climate Exposure and Health Risk

Aphiwe Ngcobo (Honours Statistics) is examining how extreme heat, drought, and heavy rainfall affect vulnerable populations in Gauteng, combining climate data with public health analysis. Expected completion: December 2026

Multivariate Methods for High-Dimensional Data

Lazola Ntanjana (MSc Statistics) is developing a Generalised Singular Value Decomposition (GSVD) approach to MANOVA for high-dimensional data. Expected completion: February 2027.

Forecasting South African Electricity Prices

Awelani Phaswana (MSc Statistics) is developing multivariate approaches for forecasting electricity prices in South Africa, combining time series methodology with the realities of the energy market. Expected completion: December 2027.

Goodness-of-Fit for Canonical Variate Analysis Biplots

Jessie Leukes (MSc Statistics) is developing measures of fit for Canonical Variate Analysis biplots based on the Generalised Singular Value Decomposition, providing robust diagnostics for assessing how well these biplots represent the underlying data structure. Expected completion: December 2027.

Risk Set Sampling in Random Survival Forests

Nontsikelelo Wittes (Honours Data Science) is investigating the effect of risk set sampling on Random Forest Survival models in the presence of censoring, examining how sampling choices at each event time influence model performance and stability.

Deep Learning for ESG Scores and Risk Measures

Steven Mphaya (PhD Statistical Data Science) is developing deep learning methods for modelling ESG scores and risk measures, exploring how neural network architectures can capture the complex, multidimensional relationships underlying sustainability ratings and their implications for financial risk.

Should I Trust My Sell-Side Analyst?

Daniel Morris and Jonathan Stagman (Honours Actuarial Science) are investigating the reliability of sell-side analyst forecasts and recommendations.

Natural Disaster Impacts on Residential Property Prices

Gianluca Caldeira and Rhys Meyer (Honours Actuarial Science) are investigating how natural disasters affect residential property prices in South Africa, using the 2017 Knysna fires and the KwaZulu-Natal floods as case studies.

Multi-Hazard Climate Risk and Parametric Insurance

Dinal Bhoola and Wade Reddy (Honours Actuarial Science) are developing a multi-hazard climate risk assessment for South Africa and evaluating parametric insurance structures as a mechanism for transferring climate risk.

Pricing European Commodity Options Using Normalising Flows

Keletso Mabelane (MSc Statistics) is developing normalising flow methods for pricing European commodity options, moving beyond restrictive distributional assumptions to capture the complex behaviour of commodity price dynamics.

Towards More Reliable Seasonal Climate Forecasts

Zahir Nikraftar (PhD Computer Science, Queen Mary University of London) is developing deep learning methods for bias correction of seasonal forecasting models, with the aim of improving the reliability of climate forecasts used in risk assessment across Africa. His related work with Prof. Rendani Mbuvha on impact-based skill evaluation of seasonal precipitation forecasts appeared in Earth's Future (2024).

Advancing Seasonal Weather Risk Assessment Using Machine Learning

Annine Duclaire Kenne (PhD Statistics) is developing machine learning methods to improve seasonal weather risk assessment, building on her earlier work on drought prediction over Cameroon and her research on deep learning for climate applications.

Climate Health Nexus

Abdoulaye Diop (PhD Statistics, University of Manchester) is researching the intersection of climate-related health and sustainable development, building on his WASCAL-funded work on multi-hazard risks to staple crop yields in the Sahel and his development of high-resolution precipitation forecasting pipelines for West Africa.

Forecast Skill Decay in AI-Based Weather Models

Kopano Motebu (Honours Mathematical Statistics) is statistically characterising how forecast skill decays with lead time in AI-based medium-range weather models, examining the practical limits of machine learning weather prediction.

Heat Stress Impacts on Labour Productivity and Crop Yields

Luke Cable and Luthando Zondi (Honours Actuarial Science) are examining how heat stress affects labour productivity and crop yields in South Africa, quantifying the economic and social consequences of rising temperatures.

Developing Collaborations

We are building partnerships with industry and academic institutions to expand our research capacity and create opportunities for future publications and conference presentations.

```
